summary: The labels print TUDCA or tauroursodeoxycholic acid at 250 or 500 mg with no purpose. The only trial here with a named positive primary outcome is a 34-patient ALS pilot at 2 g/day on top of riluzole (25664595), whose authors call the data preliminary. In progressive MS at 2 g/day, clinical and biomarker outcomes showed no significant differences (39447576). The stored primary biliary cirrhosis study (8674405) has no placebo arm. Obese adults (20522594) and healthy adults (27503949) gave surrogate results only at 1,750 and 1,500 mg.

population.description: 34 patients with ALS already on riluzole.

study_contexts.study_design: Double-blind placebo-controlled proof-of-principle trial with a 3-month lead-in, 54 weeks of treatment

outcomes.name: Responders (at least 15% ALSFRS-R slope improvement versus lead-in): 87% on TUDCA versus 43% on placebo (P = 0.021)
Baseline-adjusted ALSFRS-R at study end higher on TUDCA (P = 0.007)

limitations: Authors call it a pilot giving preliminary data and say TUDCA may be effective.
2 g/day is four to eight times the 250 to 500 mg these labels print.
Add-on to riluzole, so not TUDCA without background therapy.
